title: The challenge of recognition in large scientific collaborations
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03511-0

The authorship practices of large collaborations can hide individual contributions. A recognition programme developed by the LIGO Scientific Collaboration publicly documents verified contributions to research, infrastructure and community service.

title: Thermodynamic demonstration of tetracriticality and multicomponent superconductivity in UTe<sub>2</sub>
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03504-z

Prior measurements of the phase diagram of UTe2 contain a triple point that is forbidden by thermodynamics. Now, an additional phase boundary is discovered that resolves this problem and confirms multicomponent superconductivity in this material.

title: Multiparticle quantum walks in a dipole-conserving Bose–Hubbard model
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03512-z

Strong potential gradients can localize individual particles, but interactions can still generate collective motion. An experiment with ultracold atoms in a tilted lattice now shows this collective motion by tracking mobile bound states of fractons.

title: Automated inverse design of metainterfaces with tailored friction laws
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03503-0

Understanding friction between contacting surfaces is important to improve device performance. Now a method is shown to discover materials that offer on-demand frictional behaviour using inverse design based on genetic algorithms.

title: Motors use biased diffusion to shepherd diffusible proteins on microtubules
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03489-9

Microtubules are bound by active motors and passively diffusing proteins. Now it is shown that this mixture of active and passive molecules is a realization of rectified Brownian motion in active matter.

title: Imaging hot-electron Thomson cooling beyond the Boltzmann–Onsager framework
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03510-1

Classical Thomson cooling is inefficient. Now non-equilibrium energy dissipation with a breakdown of the Boltzmann–Onsager limit is demonstrated by imaging hot electrons in HgTe and HgCdTe quantum wells.

title: Order in a quantum chaotic sea
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03513-y

Experiments with a superconducting quantum processor revealed an island of regular motion within otherwise chaotic quantum many-body dynamics and used feedback to steer the dynamics towards it.

title: A simple twist to altermagnetism
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03495-x

Two-dimensional altermagnets hold promise for next-generation spintronics but remain difficult to synthesize. Now, altermagnetism has been observed in an orthogonally twisted van der Waals homostructure, opening possibilities for ultrathin devices.
